newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF says important to have stable forex.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF says important to have stable forex.

text.p: It is important for foreign exchange rates to move in a stable manner, Japan's Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told a news conference on Monday.
But he declined to comment specifically about the dollar's rise on Monday to 50-month highs against the yen.
Ogawa also said he did not expect Japan's trade surplus to rise substantially in the future.
"The decline in the surplus of trade and services over the last few years has been brought about by structural changes (in the Japanese economy). I don't think that trend will change," Ogawa said.
He added that the surplus in trade and services as a percentage of Japan's gross domestic product (GDP) was now at a level of below one percent, and the ratio was unlikely to rise above two percent.

Asked whether Japan intended to use the foreign exchange rate as a tool to manipulate the trade imbalance, Ogawa said: "It is important for the exchange rate to reflect external balances and to move in a stable manner."

Japan announced earlier on Monday that its current account surplus rose in February for the second month in a row, increasing 15.4 percent to 865.2 billion yen. The rise came amid mounting U.S. concern about a possible resurgence in the trade surplus, which had been steadily falling for a long period until recently.
Although Ogawa declined to comment on the dollar's rise on Monday, he said there were various views in the market about the outlook for the U.S. currency.

"If some people take note of the rise in the current account surplus, then the yen should strengthen rather than weaken. But if others pay attention to the interest-rate differential between the United States and Japan, then that would lead in another direction," he said.
